scope: 02_rules.md:Answered question OQ-17 — Dependency vulnerability and update policy

topics.topic: Accepted datetime inputs and timestamp normalization semantics
questions: Which supplied datetime representations are accepted, and does “stored as supplied” mean preserving fields or preserving the instant while converting to offset-naive UTC?

quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions). Calendar dates a source supplies — `document_date` of a
recognition, `payment_date` — are `date` values, kept as the supplied
calendar day: they carry no time or offset, are never converted to an
instant and never replaced by the clock's day; their accepted forms and checks, and where in an operation
its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.
judgement.why: The passage already makes “stored as supplied” preserve the instant while normalizing storage to offset-naive UTC, while the accepted wire representations and validation checks are formats and field-type contracts owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Allowed and forbidden caller-supplied Registry request context fields
questions: Which caller-supplied fields are forbidden Registry context, and which required identifiers or business facts may a request carry?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 about admissible project identifiers versus forbidden caller-supplied Registry context, and the relevant texts have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Registry-context request fields that must be rejected versus admissible project fields
quotes:
- **Trusted context.** No operation accepts a role, capability, actor id or
  Registry context from its caller as authority. Identity operations turn a
  presented credential into a `StaffActorContext`, `ViewerActorContext` or
  `ServiceActorContext`; `module:authorization_guard` turns an actor context
  and a `project_id` into an `AuthorizedProjectContext` (A4). A project-scoped
  use case receives that context, never an unchecked `project_id`, and
  re-reads the persisted principal where its own notes say so.

create_expense_from_recognition_endpoint: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST accept its non-path application input only from the explicit RecognitionExpenseCreateRequest JSON body, reject unknown body fields through the shared frozen model policy, and delegate payload.publication and payload.allocations; none of those fields may be interpreted as a query parameter.
precedent.why: The later texts distinguish project_id as the identity selector used to construct trusted context and require every undeclared request-body field, including supplied Registry facts, to be rejected rather than ignored.

topics.topic: Clock-source injection contract for read-only authentication and authorization
questions: Which receiving-state obligation ensures that read-only authentication and authorization operations that compare expires_at also receive the decided clock source rather than choosing an ambient source?

quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.

resolve_staff_session: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

_authorize_project_operation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
judgement.why: The later module boundary and operation notes require read-only session resolution and project authorization to obtain one instant from system_clock and forbid ambient host-clock reads.

topics.topic: Required witness test for single clock reads and reuse in comparisons and writes
questions: What Required test must demonstrate that each time-dependent operation reads the wall clock exactly once and reuses that same instant for validity comparisons as well as writes?
Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its source scan and one-reading viewer-entry requirements?

quotes:
Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes. An operation
reads the clock once for its own timestamps, and that one
instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp it writes (event times such as
`created_at`, `received_at`, `revoked_at`) and every current-time comparison
that decides the validity of those writes or of persisted records.

- CLK-001: all portal-owned event timestamps written by one operation, other than an
  audit record's `occurred_at`, are equal; an expiry it derives from a TTL is that instant plus its TTL, and source-supplied times, a service credential's supplied `expires_at` among them, keep their supplied values.

- CLK-002: the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and
  elapsed clocks; the elapsed clock is read once per viewer-entry request,
  only to measure the A25 rate-limit window, and its reading is never
  stored, turned into an instant or ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-001: a test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades,
  bootstrap) that its portal-owned event timestamps, other than audit
  `occurred_at`, are one instant; a test per operation deriving an expiry
  from a TTL (staff and viewer session creation) that the expiry equals
  that instant plus the configured TTL; and a test per operation receiving
  source-supplied times (snapshot import, recognition intake, photo intake,
  service credential issuance with a supplied `expires_at`, payment
  recording) that each supplied time and calendar date is stored as
  supplied, not as the clock's instant.

- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); and a
  viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.

- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].
judgement.divergence: One verifier uses a counting wall-clock source and proves that each time-dependent operation takes exactly one wall reading reused for comparisons and writes; another verifies only timestamp equality, TTL arithmetic, source-time preservation, host-clock source scanning and elapsed-clock counting, so an operation that calls the shared wall clock twice passes. The owner notices that the required verification admits a nonconforming implementation, and a caller or record reader can observe the boundary-dependent result and timestamp.
judgement.why: The Required tests never require counting wall-clock-source calls or proving that the instant used for an expiry comparison is the same instant used for writes, and no tagged witness is bound to CLK-002.

witness.initial: A valid staff session expires at 10:00:00.500, and a project mutation implementation calls the shared wall-clock source separately for authorization and for its event timestamp.
events: At 10:00:00.400, the staff caller starts the authorized project mutation and the operation reads the wall clock for the session-expiry comparison.
At 10:00:00.600, the operation reads the wall clock again and writes its sole portal-owned event timestamp.

The owner runs an implementation of the stated Required tests that checks timestamp equality, TTL arithmetic, supplied-time preservation, direct host-clock calls and elapsed-clock readings, but does not count wall-clock-source calls.
outcomes: A verifier that counts wall-clock-source calls rejects the implementation because the operation read twice and did not reuse one instant.
A verifier limited to the stated assertions accepts the implementation because its sole written event timestamp has no unequal companion and no module read a host clock directly.
witness.observer: The owner running the required verification; the mutation caller and a later record reader can also observe the stored 10:00:00.600 timestamp.
basis:
Every project-scoped operation evaluates, in order: valid unexpired
unrevoked session → principal status `active` → project access (viewer grant / staff assignment semantics / producer
scope) → required capability from R2 → Registry lifecycle policy (R5).

Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes. An operation
reads the clock once for its own timestamps, and that one
instant supplies every portal-owned timestamp it writes (event times such as
`created_at`, `received_at`, `revoked_at`) and every current-time comparison
that decides the validity of those writes or of persisted records.

- CLK-001: a test per multi-write operation (activation, revocation cascades,
  bootstrap) that its portal-owned event timestamps, other than audit
  `occurred_at`, are one instant; a test per operation deriving an expiry
  from a TTL (staff and viewer session creation) that the expiry equals
  that instant plus the configured TTL; and a test per operation receiving
  source-supplied times (snapshot import, recognition intake, photo intake,
  service credential issuance with a supplied `expires_at`, payment
  recording) that each supplied time and calendar date is stored as
  supplied, not as the clock's instant.

- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source calls
  a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`,
  `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants); and a
  viewer-entry test with a counting clock source that one request takes
  exactly one elapsed reading, that the window decision at its boundary
  follows that reading, and that no record written by the request holds
  it.

topics.topic: Value of completed_work_total when sections have no progress records
questions: When an active budget has sections but none has a progress record, is project-level completed_work_total zero or unavailable?

judgement.why: This is the same question P4 answered on the same unchanged passages: absent per-section values are excluded from the sum, making completed_work_total the Decimal empty sum while overall progress is unavailable.

precedent.topic: Aggregate progress and completed-work semantics when every progress record is missing
quotes:
- `completed_work_total` (here and in `BudgetView`) is the sum of the
  sections' `completed_work_value` that are not `None`; a section without a
  progress record is left out of the sum, as it is left out of overall
  progress (A9).

- Overall progress: `Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)` over
  sections of the active version with `work_planned > 0` and a recorded
  progress (a section without a progress record is left out of both sums);
  undefined (shown unavailable) when the denominator is 0.
precedent.why: The completed-work total is the empty sum when every per-section value is absent, while overall progress is unavailable whenever the filtered denominator is zero.

topics.topic: Whether remediation of a vulnerable transitive dependency requires changing a direct pin
questions: If a vulnerable transitive distribution is replaced by a fixed compatible version when the image is rebuilt with unchanged direct pins, may that new passing image deploy, or must some direct pin still change?

quotes:
An image in which a distribution has a known vulnerability is not deployed until the
   pin is updated through the Factory route.

- DEP-002: no deploy starts the service from an image in which an
  installed distribution — a pin or a library pip resolves for it — has a
  known vulnerability listed in OSV for its version.
judgement.divergence: A freshly rebuilt image whose transitive distribution is fixed while all direct pins remain unchanged is deployable under DEP-002 because the image contains no affected distribution, but remains blocked under rule 3 because no pin was updated through the Factory route; the deployment operator observes whether the service starts.
judgement.why: Rule 3 makes a Factory-route pin update a necessary remediation, while DEP-002 makes absence of an affected installed distribution in the checked image the deploy condition.

bases.passage:
An image in which a distribution has a known vulnerability is not deployed until the
   pin is updated through the Factory route.

- DEP-002: no deploy starts the service from an image in which an
  installed distribution — a pin or a library pip resolves for it — has a
  known vulnerability listed in OSV for its version.

unsupported_sides:
An image in which a distribution has a known vulnerability is not deployed until the
   pin is updated through the Factory route.

- DEP-002: no deploy starts the service from an image in which an
  installed distribution — a pin or a library pip resolves for it — has a
  known vulnerability listed in OSV for its version.

witness.initial: The deployment requirements contain an exact direct pin P, and an image built from it contains transitive distribution T version 1, which a current non-withdrawn OSV entry lists as affected.
events: The deployment operator checks the image against OSV and blocks it.
A compatible T version 2 that is not affected is released.
The deployment operator rebuilds from the unchanged direct requirements, and dependency resolution installs T version 2.
The deploy checks every distribution in the new image against fresh OSV data and obtains a passing verdict.
outcomes: DEP-002 allows the new image to start because no installed distribution has a known vulnerability.
Rule 3 refuses the new image because no pin was updated through the Factory route.
basis:
1. The deployed portal runs only the externally maintained libraries pinned
   exactly in the Factory deployment
   (`projects/client_portal_sandbox/deploy/requirements.txt`: fastapi,
   pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn), each a direct import of the deployed
   source; the pinned versions are those of that file.

3. A deploy is the start of the service from a built image. Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read in that
   same deploy; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is reused.

- DEP-001: every library from outside its own source that the running
  portal imports directly is pinned to one exact version in the deployment
  requirements; the libraries pip resolves for them are not pinned.

- DEP-002: the deploy step judges every distribution installed in the
  built image, bound to that image's content id, against OSV data read in
  the same deploy, and starts the service only on a passing verdict about
  that same image; a listed version, unreadable or unmatchable advisory
  data, a verdict from an earlier deploy, or a verdict about another image
  does not start it
  [witness: verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal].
